question: Select the correct representation as Tolerance size for a hole from the given options.
solution:
The correct answer is __50H8.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• 50H8__ represents the tolerance size for a hole.
 
• The "50" refers to the nominal size of the hole in millimeters.
 
• The "H8" indicates the tolerance grade for the hole, as per ISO standards.
 
• "H" specifies the fundamental deviation, which means the tolerance zone is located at the nominal size and only allows for oversize deviations.
 
• "8" represents the grade or accuracy level of the tolerance, with lower numbers indicating tighter tolerances.
 
• In this case, the tolerance zone lies above the nominal size, making it ideal for engineering fits.
 
• This designation is commonly used in mechanical engineering for specifying fits and clearances between parts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Fit Types:**

 
 
• Clearance fit: Always ensures a gap between mating parts.
 
• Interference fit: Mating parts are forced together with no gap.
 
• Transition fit: May result in either clearance or interference, depending on tolerances.
 
 
 
• **ISO Tolerance System:**
 
 
• Defines standard tolerances for holes and shafts to ensure interchangeability.
 
• Includes 18 grades (e.g., IT01, IT0, IT1 to IT16) for precision levels.
